ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $2.74 to the rider for the unexempted detour distance; retain the remaining metered fare and the $0.11 waiting unit.
ruling.reasoning:
RydeTAXI is a metered service, so extra distance reaches the fare; the trace confirms one off-route segment exists on this trip, F3, and the fare record shows the metered structure (distance $14.95 for 10.60 km, i.e. $1.4104/km) [F3][F4][F7][RD-1][RD-2]. RD-1 makes F3 reviewable segment by segment, and RD-4 cannot excuse it: the trace records no qualifying incident on the replaced stretch (✗ RD-4(a)), and F12 only gives an AYE speed band of 2 (10–19 km/h, 14:10–14:28) at the same time as F13/F14 show the alternatives running at bands 5 and 4 [F12][F13][F14][F15][RD-4].

Consent under RD-5 must be a RIDER message sent before the segment began. F8 (driver proposal) is 14:30, F9 (rider "Sure, no problem.") is 14:31, while F3 begins 14:28, so no rider message precedes the segment; the driver's after-the-trip statement F11 that he told the rider first is a claim, not rider-sent consent, and does not establish it [F3][F8][F9][F11][RD-5].

Even if F9 were timely, its scope is a SPECIFIC named road: the driver asked "can I go round via Clementi Road?" and the rider's words accept only that named road; nothing in the fact table ties F3 to Clementi Road — the driver's own statement names Clementi Road, not the driven path — and nothing places the segment elsewhere, so the correspondence is undetermined rather than exempt [F3][F8][F9][F11][RD-5]. Because the timing element is independently settled against the driver (✗ for "rider message sent before 14:28:45"), this undetermined scope does not leave the outcome in doubt: the segment remains unexempted and the refund is computable.

RD-3 does not apply: no stop was measured in F3 and the record contains no rider message naming a place at which the car stopped, so there is no rider-named-stop exemption [F3][F8][F9][RD-3]. There is likewise no driver errand to weigh separately — F3 is a continuous 3.07 km drive with no stop recorded [F3][F4][RD-1].

Amount, per RD-2 and the trace formula: unexempted extra_km × this trip's per-km rate = 1.94 km × ($14.95 ÷ 10.60 km = $1.4104/km) = $2.7362 → $2.74 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2]. The 0.26 km residual between the billed excess $3.06 (2.17 km) and the segment's 1.94 km is unclassified mileage and is not refunded under RD-2; the metro waiting unit $0.11 stays with the driver under RD-3(c), and base, time and platform components stand [F4][F5][F7][RD-2][RD-3].

RD-6 is not triggered: F18 shows route_disputes_upheld_90d = 0, so the profile facts cannot support a repeated-breach account flag and, in any event, profile facts never decide the case alone [F17][F18][RD-6].

segment_findings.reason: The off-route segment ran 14:28–14:34 (F3), but the driver's proposal is 14:30 (F8) and the only rider message, 'Sure, no problem.', is 14:31 (F9); RD-5 requires the rider's consent message to be timestamped before the segment start, which no message satisfies, and the driver's post-trip statement F11 is not rider-sent consent. (The scope of F9 is at most the named road Clementi Road, which nothing ties to this segment — at best undetermined under RD-5/G13 — but the timing element alone already leaves the segment unexempted.) Apart from that, no RD-3 stop was measured and RD-4(a) has no incident (F15), so the extra_km is refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: The claimed pre-segment agreement fails: the rider's message F9 is 14:31 and the proposal F8 is 14:30, both after the F3 segment start of 14:28, so RD-5's 'before the segment' element is not met.

The undetermined correspondence between the named road and the driven path does not create an exemption; RD-5 withholds the exemption unless the agreed road is tied to the segment, and independently the consent was not sent before F3 began [F3][F8][F9].

F12 (AYE band 2, 10–19 km/h) is corroborative only under RD-4(b) and cannot exempt the segment on its own; F13/F14 concern other roads and F15 records no qualifying incident under RD-4(a) [F12][F13][F14][F15].
The driver's concession that RD-4(a) is unavailable means RD-4(c) applies: with no incident, the segment is handled under RD-2, not left as no_action [F15][F3].

The arithmetic frame is accepted only in part: the $0.11 waiting unit and the base/time/platform components are retained (RD-3(c), F5, F7), but the $3.06 billed excess (2.17 km, F4) is not the refund measure — RD-2 refunds the segment's 1.94 km extra_km, i.e. $2.74 [F3][F4][F7].
Accepted as far as it goes and consistent with the ruling: F18 shows 0 route disputes upheld in 90 days, so RD-6's flag condition is not met and no account flag is issued [F18][RD-6].

The scope point is accepted as an undetermined reading of the named road (nothing ties F3 to Clementi Road) but it does not change the outcome: the timing element under RD-5 already fails, so the segment counts and the amount is determined by the trace formula [F3][F8][F9][RD-2][RD-5].
